Accurate PSF modelling matters. Biases in PSF estimation feed straight into cosmic shear measures, a main probe of cosmic expansion and structure growth for dark energy studies. PIFF builds models per CCD alone, losing coherence across the focal plane. The new hybrid model trains an autoencoder on HSC star images and pairs it with a Gaussian process to fill in the PSF across the full field. It reaches a rebuild error of 3.4 times ten to the minus six against PIFF 3.7, laying groundwork for LSST pipelines.
arxiv-2602-15880:
Bian and colleagues join Newton-type thresholding with ReLU methods for sparse signal recovery with no negative values. Such recovery has wide uses and a long research history. Recent work has used rectified linear units to boost older recovery methods.

The team offers two methods. The first is Newton-Direction-Based ReLU-Thresholding, or NDRT. The second is its stronger form, Newton-Direction-Based ReLU-Thresholding Pursuit, or NDRTP. Theory shows both can recover such signals exactly when the measure matrix meets a set condition. Tests show NDRTP matching top rivals in both noisy and noiseless cases.
arxiv-2602-16580:
Fabian Faulstich and co-authors extend algebro-geometric results for coupled cluster theory. They study the doubles truncation variety for four electrons, the first genuinely nonlinear doubles regime. This variety differs from earlier studied ones. The paper opens a systematic study of its basic invariants, mixing theory with numerical evidence. For four electrons on enough orbitals, the variety is a complete intersection of a stated degree. A Pfaffian structure lies behind its quadratic relations.

An exact tensor product factorization holds in a limit of disconnected doubles. The structural results are tied to a small but hard test case. That case is beryllium insertion into molecular hydrogen, where multiconfigurational effects run strong. Quantum chemists and algebraic geometers get new exact structure for a workhorse approximation method.
arxiv-2602-17180:
Alexander Setescak led an eleven-author team turning a hard magnetic imaging problem into a tractable one. Rebuilding magnetization textures from nitrogen-vacancy stray-field data is ill-posed at heart, and the sensor-to-sample gap is usually unknown. The paper builds a micromagnetic energy term directly into the inversion, filtering out unphysical high-energy layouts.

Fourier-space upward continuation of the stray field then lets the gap be fitted at the same time. Applied to the van der Waals ferromagnet iron gallium telluride, the method found a plausible gap size and low-energy layouts matching the observed field. More broadly, building physics into rebuilding makes magnetic inverse problems clear and interpretable, with uses well beyond nitrogen-vacancy magnetometry.
arxiv-2602-17280:
Arshia Dutta led a two-author study of how refugees and asylum seekers in the UK experience border control and the wider immigration system, and how those encounters shape later life. Through observation in a support organization plus talks with caseworkers, asylum seekers, and refugees, the paper traces the long shadow of the first border meeting combined with a hostile system.

Those interviewed described insecurity, anxiety, and doubt that lingered well beyond arrival, coloring their sense of belonging. The authors add to human-computer interaction work on the tensions between immigration and security technology. They point toward joint design work that centers the lived experience and everyday security of asylum seekers and refugees, rather than treating them as cases to process.
arxiv-2602-17380:
Jureeporn Yuennan led a four-author team testing beta-exponential inflation against the latest Atacama Cosmology Telescope data. Recent ACT data plus DESI baryon data point to a scalar spectral index higher than the Planck 2018 value, straining attractor models. The paper tests the beta-exponential potential, which extends standard models and arises in braneworld settings, in both coupled forms.

Slow-roll values and observables come from a small series in the non-minimal coupling, checked by computer. In the simple case, the model predicts a spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio within ACT plus DESI constraints while yielding a tilt larger than the attractor forecast. Adding small coupling lifts the fit further by cutting the tensor-to-scalar ratio while keeping the raised tilt, in line with ACT, DESI, and BICEP/Keck bounds. That model thus agrees well with the latest cosmic background data.
arxiv-2602-17480:
Fernando Rafael Chu Rivera led a two-author team presenting Twisted Type Theory, a new directed type theory. Homotopy Type Theory has done well as a base for maths and a language for spaces, also called infinity-groupoids. Yet in much of maths and computing, categories matter more than groupoids. Several directed theories have been put forward, with meaning based on categories.

Its twist turns a type leaning on variables in both directions into one leaning on them in a single direction only. For that step's meaning, the authors build dependent two-sided fibrations, widening a notion due to Street. They lay out their basic theory and pin them down with a straightening-unstraightening theorem. A new elimination rule for Hom-types follows. The paper closes by proving Yoneda's lemma in syntactic form, showing the theory can reason about categories in a Homotopy Type Theory-like style.
arxiv-2602-17780:
Pedro Gil and Vladimir Konotop study groups of pinned modes of Bose-Einstein condensates, or BECs, in a one-dimensional optical cavity. The BEC sits under an outside field plus atom-cavity coupling with jointly incommensurate periods. That setup localizes matter waves even with no two-body forces, a striking effect the paper maps in detail.

Within the mean-field view, the authors study pinned modes for red and blue detunings from atomic and cavity resonances in fairly shallow quasiperiodic lattices, beyond tight-binding validity. They identify settings supporting localization of atomic wave packets. Two types of bistability appear as distinct photon numbers under else identical settings: one from coexisting mode groups, typical of closed systems, and one from many-valued setting links, typical of hysteresis. A two-mode setup can act as an XOR logic gate.
arxiv-2602-17880:
Ilias Ourahou and team directly measure three-dimensional deuteron track recoils from neutron capture in hydrogen with the MIMAC-35 cm detector. Neutron capture concerns most detector nuclei. It produces protons, alpha particles and gamma rays as background signals. Characterizing that background matters for rare event searches such as dark matter detection and coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering.

Data were collected over more than five days in a chamber about thirty-five by thirty-five by twenty-nine centimeters. The gas mix was seventy percent isobutane and thirty percent trifluoromethane. A method based on three-dimensional tracks and released ionization energy separates nuclear recoils from the dominant electron recoil background. It clearly identifies low-energy deuteron tracks from hydrogen capture. Fifty-one neutron capture events were observed among over eleven million total events, mostly muon-produced, showing MIMAC's power for low-energy rare events with huge background and no shielding.
arxiv-2602-18080:
Fran Ilčić and team report a quantum simulation of hadron motion in a one-plus-one-dimensional SU-two lattice gauge theory, on an IBM processor. Real-time evolution of strongly linked matter remains a frontier. Classical runs struggle with exponential Hilbert space and rapid entanglement growth.

With a hardware-friendly Loop-String-Hadron encoding, the team simulates the physical degrees of freedom on a sixty-site lattice in the weak-coupling regime, toward the continuum limit. The hardware data reveal confined meson propagation and early oscillations of the mesonic profile, yielding a breathing-mode frequency as an observable. Tensor-network simulations of the encoding Hamiltonian support the physical approximation and the quantum algorithm. Pauli-propagation simulations of the noiseless circuit support the observed dynamics in the accessible window. The results show physics-native encodings can open scalable access to coherent non-Abelian dynamics on noisy hardware.
arxiv-2602-18180:
Fatemeh Taghipoor and three co-authors push quantum teleportation toward near-perfect fidelity with a new resource. Standard continuous-variable teleportation, built on squeezed vacuum states, can never quite reach perfect fidelity. The team instead tests three-level entangled states, called qutrits, under realistic noise.

Their scheme holds up well both in clean theory and in noisy conditions, moving continuous-variable states with high fidelity and a fair chance of success. That mix matters: lab gear is never ideal, so a method that only shines without noise helps little. The paper points to qutrit resources as a practical route to faithful quantum state transfer.
arxiv-2602-18280:
Lucas Alves Zischler and four co-authors extend spontaneous Raman scattering models to space-division multiplexing fibers. Their 2026 paper notes this weak nonlinear effect matters for mixing classical and quantum signals and for sensing. Recent work on stimulated Raman scattering in such fibers offers a bridge, since the two effects are intrinsically linked.

The team generalizes single-mode fiber models to fibers with several mode groups of same-frequency modes. Both Stokes and anti-Stokes bands are covered. The resulting tool needs no fiber-specific design details to estimate scattered noise in optical links. Tests in field-deployed multi-core fibers and multi-mode fiber agree well with the model. Network designers gain a portable way to budget Raman noise in next-generation links.
arxiv-2602-18580:
Mickael V. S. de Farias and four co-authors constrain long-lived particles with cosmology. Their 2026 paper notes long-lived particles offer a window into physics beyond the Standard Model, with distinct signatures at colliders and in cosmology. The team investigates long-lived decays into dark matter.

If lifetimes exceed ten thousand seconds, decay products can disrupt synthesis of light nuclei in the early cosmos and change Big Bang Nucleosynthesis predictions. If the particle is much heavier than dark matter, decay contributes to the effective number of neutrino species. The team describes these decays via dimension-six operators and outlines the parameter space where such decays obey cosmological bounds from nucleosynthesis, structure formation, cosmic microwave background, and baryon oscillation data.
arxiv-2602-18980:
In Funk geometry, the lines splitting space between sites are strikingly simple. Aditya Acharya, with three co-authors, studies Voronoi diagrams in 2026 in polygonal and elliptical cones, under forward and reverse Funk metrics. Funk metrics are basic distance functions on convex bodies, underpinning the Hilbert and Thompson metrics.

First findings are about shape. Bisectors form rays that start at the cone apex. A diagram in d dimensions matches an additively-weighted diagram in one fewer dimension on a bounded cross section. That match yields a route for elliptical cones through Apollonius diagrams, with running time O(n^{ceil((d-1)/2)+1}). Another route covers three-dimensional polygonal cones with m facets through abstract Voronoi diagrams, in O(mn log(n)) time. A full account of when three sites share a circumcenter in three-dimensional cones ends one of the first algorithmic studies of Funk metrics.
arxiv-2602-19380:
Tracking the glottic opening in video laryngoscopy is hard: single-frame finders lack time context, while base-model trackers drift as memory corrupts. Huayu Wang and seven co-authors propose Closed-Loop Memory Correction. In this detector-in-the-loop design, a detector supervises the Segment Anything Model 2 tracker through confidence-aligned state choices and active memory repair. Rapid tissue shifting, occlusions, and visual confusion in emergency settings make such stability essential.

High-confidence hits trigger semantic resets, overwriting corrupted tracker memory and curbing drift without training a new tracker. On emergency airway videos, the method reaches state-of-the-art results, with much less drift and a lower missing rate compared with SAM2 variants and open-loop methods. The paper shows memory correction as crucial for reliable clinical video tracking.
arxiv-2602-19580:
Jeremy McEntire offers Leap+Verify, a framework that runs guess-ahead work in neural network training: future weights get guessed, then checked before they count. Borrowing from guess-ahead decoding for language model use and from the Automatically Scalable Computation design, it splits training into three auto-spotted phases: chaotic, transition, and stable. Activation-space cosine closeness serves as a live Lyapunov proxy.

Within each phase, math guessers (momentum, linear, quadratic curve-fits) forecast weights K steps ahead, with guesses kept only after checks against a held-out loss bar. Tests use GPT-2 124M and Qwen 2.5-1.5B, both trained on WikiText-103, with five random seeds. Guess depth K runs over 5, 10, 25, 50, 75, and 100 steps, testing when guessing pays.
arxiv-2602-19780:
Lead-free halide materials based on cesium and copper glow brightly and stay stable in air, but devices built from them lose much light to poor outcoupling. A 2026 arXiv paper by Shoumik Debnath and four co-authors studies how halide composition shapes plasmon-enhanced emission, combining quantum-mechanical calculations with optical simulations.

Computed refractive indices and extinction spectra feed full three-dimensional simulations of a light-emitting stack with silver-silica core-shell nanostructures. The chloride composition gives the strongest plasmonic response and the best light extraction with optimized nanorods, helped by its lower refractive index. The bromide shows the best spectral overlap but more confinement, while the iodide needs a nanosphere shape and gains least. The paper yields composition-specific design rules for lead-free devices.
arxiv-2602-19980:
Language models that generate token by token often struggle with planning tasks that demand looking several steps ahead. A 2026 arXiv paper by Itamar Trainin and three co-authors compares autoregressive models with non-autoregressive discrete diffusion models on such lookahead tasks.

The key asymmetry is that forward generation must make hard choices at branching points, while reverse generation is often fixed. Diffusion models exploit that asymmetry: analysis of mechanisms shows they learn to decode backwards using future tokens, sidestepping complex traversal machinery entirely. Both model families reach perfect accuracy on the lookahead task studied, but diffusion models need far fewer training examples and shallower designs. Left-to-right models, by contrast, often fail to converge without tailored training plans.
arxiv-2602-20080:
AI policy usually proceeds by analogy. Advanced systems get treated as products, platforms, or infrastructure. The regimes overlap and clash. A 2026 arXiv paper by M. Alejandra Parra-Orlandoni and two co-authors argues this trap misses the shift. Some AI systems now act as power centres. They shape information, coordinate conduct, and structure economic life.

The paper proposes counting such systems as a social actor alongside people, the state, and enterprises, under the name Digital Gorilla. Its Four Actors framework maps power among the four actors across modalities: economic, epistemic, narrative, authoritative, and physical. That map shows where AI capabilities unsettle authority, concentrate power, or erode accountability. Separated powers and federalism inspire a federalized, many-centred architecture with checks and balances linking the four actors. The question shifts from controlling technology to designing institutions that can house systems while keeping democratic legitimacy, the rule of law, and public goods.
arxiv-2602-20180:
Sidewalk delivery robots are becoming part of urban life. That raises a critical question: is robot labor labor? A 2026 arXiv paper by EunJeong Cheon and Do Yeon Shin pursues that provocation through fieldwork in two smart-city districts in Seoul, examining how delivery robot labor is jointly sustained.

Robotic actions often look autonomous and efficient. In fact, each successful delivery is a shared feat across people and machines, depending on human work, rule-based teamwork, and social give-and-take. Delivery robots do not replace labor. They reshape it. Some forms become more visible, such as robotic performance. Others are obscured, such as human and official support. Factory robots stay in factories, but delivery robots share public space with everyday passersby and sit embedded in policy and progress stories. So their labor is a political question about public space.
arxiv-2602-20280:
Kristin DeVleming offers graduate students a route into the study of Fano varieties and their moduli. Her 2026 survey accompanies a summer bootcamp on K-stability and K-moduli held at the 2025 Summer Research Institute in Algebraic Geometry. Moduli problems ask how geometric objects can be organized into families and classified, and Fano varieties form one important class of such objects.

The survey supplies the background a newcomer needs to start research on explicit K-moduli problems. It explains K-stability and K-moduli, the ideas behind classifying Fano varieties by their stability properties. Written for readers new to the area, it bridges general background and the open, concrete problems that researchers now pursue. Its aim is to leave a newcomer ready to work on specific examples rather than only general theory.
arxiv-2602-20380:
Rodrigo Nicolau Almeida and two co-authors prove that the variety of modal lattices has the superamalgamation property. Superamalgamation, in this setting, is a strong form of the amalgamation property for these structures. Their 2026 paper works with the recent duality for modal lattices based on modal L-spaces. As a consequence, the weak positive modal logic gains the Craig interpolation property.

The authors extend the result to a number of other weak positive modal logics, those axiomatized by modal axioms matching universal Horn sentences. The extension shows the duality method reaches beyond a single logic. For readers, the result links an algebraic property of lattices to a logical property of proofs: superamalgamation on one side, interpolation on the other. It gives modal logicians a route for lifting interpolation results across related weak positive systems.
arxiv-2602-20480:
Flow models and two-way neural networks share nice traits, two-way mapping and tractable Jacobians, yet theory has lagged on how well they near under real givens. Shubhanshu Shekhar and four co-authors offer VINA, a unified setup for two-way networks and flow models. It builds on variational unsupervised loss functions, drawn from related forms for generative adversarial networks and precision-recall divergence training. Within it, they derive result promises for output accuracy in two-way networks and spread accuracy in flow models.

The givens behind these promises are weaker and more practical than prior work needed. Wide case studies distill general design rules and usable tips from the theory. The authors close by demonstrating the approach on a realistic ocean-acoustic inversion problem, showing the framework's value beyond abstract guarantees.
arxiv-2602-20580:
Modern language models train on huge web scrapes holding millions of personal information instances, many of which the models memorize. Nishant Subramani and two co-authors build a detector suite of regexes and rules for email addresses, phone numbers, and IP addresses that beats the best regex-based detectors. On a hand-curated set of four hundred eighty-three personal information instances, they measure how often models parrot the data verbatim when prompted with the preceding tokens.

The Pythia-6.9b model parrots nearly fourteen percent of the instances exactly under greedy decoding. Across the Pythia suite, from the smallest to the largest models and across training steps, both model size and training amount track positively with memorization. Even the smallest model, Pythia-160m, parrots under three percent exactly. The paper strongly urges that pretraining data be aggressively filtered and anonymized to cut such parroting.
arxiv-2602-20780:
Jose Carlos Pelayo and one co-author study a one-dimensional Bose-Hubbard model that starts as a doubly occupied density wave. At strong interactions, the motion is ruled by doublon-holon swaps, which create a moving domain wall and a flipped, staggered pattern in density correlations.

Single-particle and pair correlations stay tightly local. They fade fast beyond nearest neighbors. The wall moves on a time scale set by the inverse interaction strength, slowing relaxation. A parabolic trap freezes motion at the edges and curbs spreading further. At strong coupling the model maps onto an antiferromagnetic transverse-field Ising model. Its spin waves match the spread speed.
arxiv-2602-21080:
Rebuilding DNA without a reference means aligning overlapping fragments, a combinatorial task often cast as binary optimization. Pedro Prado and eight co-authors test quantum feedback methods for that job in this 2026 arXiv paper. They focus on three versions of the feedback-based algorithm, which removes classical optimization loops through measurement feedback.

Long-read fragments from SARS-CoV-2 and human mitochondrial DNA are analyzed with standard, second-order, and time-rescaled FALQON. The two newer versions reach the ground state faster and succeed more often even with shallower circuits. The findings suggest feedback-driven quantum dynamics can handle combinatorial problems on near-term hardware.
arxiv-2602-21180:
Data systems recall by design, yet oversight more and more demands believable loss. Viktoriia Makovska, George Fletcher, Julia Stoyanovich, and Tetiana Zakharchenko argue loss is not one move in this 2026 arXiv paper, but a social-plus-tech practice with distinct tools. They split erasure, un-training, and shut-out under loss as a cover term.

Erasure takes away or blocks access to items, un-training bounds or takes away a data point's sway on models, and shut-out means upstream not gathering. Loss spans agency, timing, can-it-be-undone, and scale, and it can guard rights while also allowing muting. The authors propose treating un-training as a first-class skill judged by openness, being held to account, and knowledge fairness, not only rule-following.
arxiv-2602-21280:
A deep all-sky infrared survey would serve astronomy for decades, and the Roman Space Telescope could deliver it. A large team led by Jiwon Jesse Han lays out a feasible path in this 2026 arXiv white paper, imaging the entire sky at about a tenth of an arcsecond resolution. The plan starts with high-impact fields in the first cycle and scales to ultra-wide coverage within the nominal mission.

The first-epoch survey reaches faint magnitudes while preserving time for other ambitious programs, and an example first-cycle program triples early Roman-LSST overlap. Community products would include forced photometry, joint astrometry, and catalogs of galactic substructure, strong lenses, and rare systems. The paper invites broad community participation in shaping the survey.
arxiv-2602-21480:
Germán T. Eizaguirre and two co-authors ask how good language-model agents are at Text-to-Big SQL. Text-to-SQL and Big Data are each heavily benchmarked. But little work evaluates them jointly, even though real Text-to-SQL systems sit inside Big Data workflows like large-scale processing.

Existing benchmarks stay narrowly scoped and ignore cost and performance at scale. Small translation errors barely matter on tiny datasets but create large cost and latency overheads on big ones. The authors introduce new metrics for Text-to-Big SQL and evaluate frontier models. Standard Text-to-SQL metrics prove insufficient for Big Data, while the new metrics track efficiency, cost, and scale effects. One model trades about 7 percent lower accuracy for up to about 12 times faster speed. A later model proves more than twice as cost-effective as a rival at large input scales.
arxiv-2602-21580:
Naomi Ota and ten co-authors measure bulk and churn motions in the merging galaxy cluster Abell 3395 South using XRISM. High-detail X-ray spectra with XRISM/Resolve study the iron XXV helium-alpha glow, straight measuring line-of-sight bulk and churn speeds of the in-cluster medium.

One-dimensional churn speed proves low, about 124 kilometres per second, while a large bulk speed of about 263 km/s is found. Low churn mixed with finite bulk motion suggests the subcluster has not yet reached a settled state. The results fit the absence of a radio halo, implying churn re-boost is currently weak in the core. The study shows XRISM spectra can straight constrain in-cluster medium motion in merging clusters and gives a benchmark for future side-by-side studies of Abell 3395 North and Abell 3391.
arxiv-2602-21680:
David Eckel and one co-author introduce the Hierarchical Lead Critic for multi-agent reward-based learning. Team reward-based learning solves complex tasks needing coordination from multiple agents, but it often sticks to either local independent learning or global centralized learning views.

The paper offers a novel sequential training scheme and design learning from multiple views on different levels. The Hierarchical Lead Critic draws inspiration from natural emerging distributions in team structures, where following high-level objectives combines with low-level execution. Introducing multiple levels, leveraging local and global views, can improve performance with high sample efficiency and robust policies. Tests on team, non-communicative, and partially observable benchmarks show the Hierarchical Lead Critic beating single-level baselines and scaling robustly with rising agent counts and difficulty.
arxiv-2602-22080:
Classifying finite skew braces up to isomorphism is a major open problem in their structural theory. Marco Damele and Vicent Pérez Calabuig take up a classic question within that project: does a Cauchy theorem hold for finite skew braces? Such a theorem would guarantee elements of prime order, in the spirit of the classic Cauchy theorem for groups.

The proof covers finite two-sided skew braces and bi-skew braces, with consequences and related structural results sketched alongside. The result does not settle the question for all finite skew braces, but it secures two large territories where the familiar group-theoretic pattern holds. Algebraists gain firmer footing for the wider classification project.
arxiv-2602-22180:
Comets beyond our solar system shed material under wildly different suns, winds, and stellar ages, yet they are often treated as copies of our own comets. Théo Vrignaud and seven co-authors review what drives mass loss from these exocomets and what happens to the released material next. At home, small bodies lose mass through sublimation, desorption, impacts, and sputtering, and the ejecta then evolve under dust sublimation, ionization, and radiation pressure.

Around other stars, those same mechanisms play out under far harsher and more varied radiative and plasma conditions, producing a rich diversity of mass-loss paths and observable signatures. The review gathers a field where processes remain poorly constrained despite decades of observations. Readers get a structured map of how exocomet tails and gas come to be, and where the open questions lie.
arxiv-2602-22480:
Coding agents are increasingly used to improve other agents, but the field lacks a systematic picture of how well that works. Varun Ursekar and four co-authors note that harness optimization differs from ordinary software work. Agent harnesses mix fixed code with random language-model outputs, so both step-by-step traces and final outcomes must be captured in structured form. They introduce VeRO, an outer harness for versioned snapshots, budget-controlled evaluation, and structured traces of target harnesses.

Alongside it comes VeRO-Bench, a suite of target agents and tasks with reference evaluation procedures. Using VeRO, the team runs an empirical study comparing optimizers across tasks and asking which edits reliably improve target harnesses. The team makes VeRO publicly available so research into agent optimization can develop as a central competence for coding agents.
arxiv-2602-22680:
Yue Xu and seven co-authors survey personalized agents powered by large language models. As agents reason, plan, and use tools over long interactions, success hinges on adapting to each user and carrying context across sessions. Personalization then runs through the whole decision pipeline, not just surface wording.

The survey organizes prior work around four linked capabilities: profile modelling, memory, planning, and action execution. It traces how user signals are captured, passed along, and used across those stages, flagging cross-component links and recurring design traps. Evaluation metrics, benchmarking styles, and uses from chat assistants to expert systems are also reviewed, giving builders a structured map of the field.
arxiv-2602-23180:
Marek Tyburec and two co-authors study free material optimization for flat, two-dimensional parts under in-plane stress. Two isotropic phases mix to cut flex under load. To link free design with what composites can realize, they build a ladder of admissible sets from zeroth-order, Voigt, and Hashin-Shtrikman energy bounds.

The zeroth-order and Voigt models are convex and agree at the ends of the volume budget while differing in between. The Voigt case reduces to variable-thickness-sheet design. The tighter Hashin-Shtrikman set is nonconvex, but its convex hull equals the Voigt set. Reduced formulas pin down the smallest volume fraction each bound allows. For orthotropic tensors this shrinks to a one-dimensional search over strain trace. In the single-load case the Hashin-Shtrikman optimum matches the Allaire-Kohn relaxation via sequential laminates, while for several loads the bounds stay necessary but not sufficient.
arxiv-2602-23280:
Hrishikesh Viswanath and six co-authors propose Mollified Value Learning, a steadier way to learn goal-reaching behavior from fixed data sets. Offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning struggles with value estimation when state-action coverage is thin. Physics-informed fixes impose point-by-point distance-like constraints from Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman optimality, often via the Eikonal equation, but local enforcement through point-by-point math turns unstable in complex, high-dimensional settings.

The key insight reframes distance-like constraints as an average over a local spatial measure. Averaging over the measure, rather than checking single points, acts as a spatial mollifier that builds distance-like value geometry without costly extra math. Tests on navigation and complex robot manipulation show The method learns structured value pictures and improves goal-reaching when paired with implicit value representation methods.
arxiv-2602-23780:
Alfredo González-Calvin presents an exact method for undoing a blur caused by a smooth kernel, a task known as deconvolution. The 2026 solo paper starts from a clean algebraic fact: blurring with an even Schwartz kernel maps finite-degree polynomials onto themselves, and can be inverted exactly there.

The author extends that finite inversion to wide function spaces, including integrable and square-integrable functions, smooth rapidly decaying functions, and tempered distributions. The inverse appears as a limit of finite sums of repeated blurs, so it can be computed step by step. As a main use, the method gives a new iterative formula for inverting the Weierstrass transform, sidestepping older methods that blow up small errors. It offers a robust route to signal recovery.
arxiv-2602-23880:
Zhang Wan and two co-authors develop a theory of graph classification under domain shift, viewed through random graph models. The 2026 paper treats graphs in a class as samples from a shared generative model, with shift arising when model components change. Classic domain adaptation theory handles that lens only coarsely for structured graph data.

Building on a vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert space formulation, the authors derive a generalization bound. Its shift penalty splits into three parts. One part is a domain discrepancy term. A second part is a spectral-geometry term from the accessible truncated spectrum. A third part is an amplitude term gathering convergence and construction stability. Tests on real data and simulations verify the insights carried by each term. The theory gives graph learners a finer account of why performance drops under shift and which factors drive it.
arxiv-2602-24080:
Xiang Li and seven co-authors run the first Turing test for speech-to-speech conversational systems, asking whether current systems can converse like humans. The 2026 paper collects thousands of human judgments on dialogues between nine leading speech-to-speech systems and human participants.

The verdict is clear: no evaluated system passes the test, and the gap in human-likeness is significant. A fine-grained taxonomy of human-likeness dimensions, crowd-annotated on the collected dialogues, shows the bottleneck is not semantic understanding but paralinguistic features, emotional expressivity, and conversational persona. Off-the-shelf AI judges also prove unreliable at the task. The authors answer with an interpretable model built on fine-grained human-likeness ratings, offering accurate and transparent automatic evaluation beyond a simple pass-fail verdict. In short, the voice still gives the game away.
arxiv-2603-00080: Frasch presents ResearchTwin, a free federated platform that turns a researcher's output into a chat-based digital twin for finding work. Its build links a neural layer that runs retrieval-augmented generation, a glial layer that stores and throttles requests, and a multimodal connector layer. He also sets out the S-index, a combined score built on FAIR rules that credits code and dataset work next to citations. A case study shows two scholars with near-equal H-indexes scoring far apart, and the platform offers an agent search API.
arxiv-2603-00180: Kim and colleagues present NNiT, a diffusion system that generates neural network weights without tying generation to fixed matrix sizes. It turns weight matrices into patches and models them as locally shaped fields. Graph HyperNetworks with a convolutional decoder align the weight space, creating the local links patch processing needs. On multilayer perceptrons, where permutation symmetry is sharpest, NNiTs generate working networks across architectures. On ManiSkill3 robot tasks, NNiT tops 85% success on unseen layouts while baselines fail, and the same pipeline works on MNIST classification.
arxiv-2603-00380: Zhang and 33 colleagues catalogue galaxy shapes across the Abell 2744 lensing field, measuring tens of thousands of sources in JWST imaging from the UNCOVER MegaScience survey. Single component Sérsic fits yield sizes and shape traits with random errors from posterior spreads. Robust traits emerge for most high signal sources, and size against wavelength fits give rest frame sizes in ultraviolet, optical, and near infrared bands. Injection tests bound errors, and the released catalogue spans a broad sweep of redshift, mass, and size after lensing correction.
arxiv-2603-00680: Li and nine colleagues let long horizon agents manage their own memory with MemPO, self memory policy optimisation, instead of relying on external memory lookup. The policy model summarises and curates memory during interaction, guided by credit assignment tied to memory effectiveness. Keeping only crucial information cuts token use sharply while preserving task performance. Tests confirm large F1 gains over the base model and the previous best baseline, alongside steep token reductions.
arxiv-2603-00880: Manyer, Tushar, and Badia build a shared coding framework for hybrid finite-element methods inside the Gridap library. Despite different mathematical roots, these methods share hybrid spaces, local projections, and static condensation, so the authors add graph-based mesh tools, broken polynomial spaces, and automatic condensation. The result is compact code for non-conforming polytopal methods across Poisson, elasticity, Stokes flow, and optimal control problems, kept fast by Julia compilation and lazy evaluation.
arxiv-2603-00980: Chen and seven colleagues rebuild generative recommenders around the hierarchy hidden in user behavior, which flat-sequence models ignore. Their HPGR framework first pre-trains with session-based masked item modeling to learn layered item representations, then fine-tunes with sparse attention guided by preference, focusing compute on the most relevant past items. Tests on a large industrial dataset and a live A/B experiment beat strong baselines, including HSTU and MTGR.
arxiv-2603-01080: Dash and three colleagues bring deep-learning super-resolution to turbulent reacting flows on complex meshes, where existing models mostly assume uniform grids. Their graph neural network uses message passing to rebuild small-scale structures from coarse data on non-uniform and unstructured meshes alike. Tests on a reacting channel flow and a hydrogen-fueled engine show accurate fine-scale reconstruction by visual, statistical, and cumulative-error checks, aiding coarse simulations and subgrid modeling.
arxiv-2603-01180: Chaudhuri, Ghosh, and Garain simulate outflows from an unmagnetized shocked accretion disk around a non-rotating supermassive black hole, asking whether magnetic fields are needed for collimated jets. Their thick-disk runs launch bipolar outflow from near the hole outward to about 2,651 Schwarzschild radii, reaching a top speed of 14 percent of light speed. Outflow rate tracks the infalling gas's angular momentum, and the team also computes self-Comptonized bremsstrahlung spectra for the disk-jet runs.
arxiv-2603-01580:
Arghodeep Nandi, Ojasva Saxena, and Tanmoy Chakraborty score the quality of AI reasoning traces in this 2026 work. Step-by-step traces now support math solving and fact checks, yet most scoring tools judge them in shallow ways. A good score should track how people judge sound, clear thought.

Their frame, MarODE, treats a trace as a path that evolves step by step like a Markov chain. An equation-based view of that path yields a quality score with no need to re-run the model. Tests use human-like damage to traces plus direct human ratings to check the score. MarODE beats prior baselines by a wide margin on a rank-based match with human views. The authors argue that theory-led scoring will matter more as traces sit at the core of AI systems.
arxiv-2603-01680:
Moumita Naskar, Anton Kulbakov, Kaushick Parui, and colleagues probe two crystals that may host a spin-liquid-like state. Their 2026 work studies double hydroxyperovskites, materials where magnetic frustration mixes with disordered protons. That mix can keep spins fluctuating in a quantum-disordered state instead of freezing into order.

The team used muon spin relaxation, a probe that plants muons to sense local magnetic fields. Fully deuterated samples of the copper and manganese compounds were cooled to near absolute zero. No sign of long-range magnetic order appears even at the lowest heat reached. Relaxation rates keep rising as the samples cool, which signals spins that never settle. Both compounds thus fit a dynamic, spin-liquid-like ground state steadied by proton disorder.
arxiv-2603-01780:
Zhao Yang, Hengchang Liu, Chuan Cao, and Bing Su build a DNA language model that both reads and writes sequences. Their 2026 work notes a split: masked models understand DNA well but cannot generate it, while left-to-right models generate but miss two-way context. DNA control links run both ways along the strand, so one-way reading is a real handicap.

Their model, D3LM, reuses a known transformer design but trains it as masked diffusion in discrete DNA space. Masked diffusion hides and restores chunks, which supports both grasp and generation in one model. At equal size, it beats its masked base model on understanding tasks. On regulatory element generation, its realism score nears real DNA and crushes the prior best mark. Design tests on token schemes and sampling add guidance for later DNA diffusion work.
arxiv-2603-02080:
Isaac Corley, Caleb Robinson, Inbal Becker-Reshef, and Juan Lavista Ferres test how to pool pixel embeddings into patch summaries for Earth data. Their 2026 work serves geospatial foundation models that release reusable pixel-level embedding products. Downstream tasks label whole patches or regions, so dense pixels must collapse into one representation.

Mean pooling, the default, discards within-patch variability and can falter under spatial shift. Their EuroSAT-Embed set holds tens of thousands of embedding files from three foundation models. Eleven training-free pooling methods and two fitted baselines face random and geographically disjoint test splits. Richer pooling cuts the geographic generalization gap by more than half versus mean pooling. A three-tier recommendation follows: mean as baseline, summary statistics as default, and covariance pooling for peak accuracy.
arxiv-2603-02380:
Satyam Agarwal, Alphonse Sterling, Shibu Mathew, and colleagues report a twin pair of odd solar flares in this 2026 paper. The flares erupted on April 22, 2022, inside a four-pole magnetic layout. Two active regions on the Sun formed that layout together. Space and ground telescopes tracked both flares as they evolved.

Each flare's ribbons grew longer by fresh brightenings, rather than spreading apart. That pattern marks a process called slipping reconnection. The two flares look alike and likely share a like trigger. Smaller ribbon pairs nearby may have triggered each main flare in turn. Field modeling found two boundary layers rooted near the ribbons. Many small reconnections inside those layers, firing near together, likely made the twin flares.
arxiv-2603-02480:
Athul Ashok, Owen DePoint, Jackson MacDonald, and colleagues design satellite constellations for a global quantum network in this 2026 paper. Ground quantum links face hard physical limits over long distances. Satellites can instead generate entangled photon pairs for stations worldwide. Which orbits and cluster sizes maximize that generation is the design question.

The team searches over inclination angles and how satellites split among clusters. Ground stations are fixed sets spread across the globe. Two black-box optimizers are compared: a Bayesian method and a genetic algorithm. Both reach comparable peak entanglement rates in their tests. Bayesian search often converges faster, while genetic search resists local traps better. Both crush naive designs that simply maximize ground coverage.
arxiv-2603-03080:
Chengkai Wang and Baisong Liu name a quiet failure of recommendation explanations: being right about the facts but wrong about the person. A language model can justify a suggestion with true item traits that the user's own history barely supports or even contradicts. Their 2026 paper calls these preference-inconsistent explanations and notes that hallucination checks cannot see them.

Their framework, PURE, fixes the evidence before any writing happens. It selects a compact set of reasoning paths over item structures, scored for user intent, specificity, and diversity, filtering out generic padding. Generation then follows those paths under structure-aware prompting. A new feature-level metric makes the failure measurable at last. On three real datasets, inconsistent explanations and hallucinations both fell, with accuracy intact.
arxiv-2603-03580:
Xu Yao and Lei Kang teach text-reading models to answer questions about what they read. Optical character recognition for scene text and handwriting usually jumps straight to a transcription, skipping detailed reasoning about structure. Their 2026 augmentation framework borrows from visual question answering: during training, the model must also answer generated questions about each image's text.

The questions probe character-level facts, whether a letter appears, where it sits, and how often, with answers drawn from the true transcription. That forces fine-grained reasoning and aligns visual features with textual queries. On the WordArt and Esposalles datasets, models trained this way beat their baselines consistently. Both character and word error rates fell significantly. The authors release their code publicly for other recognition researchers.
arxiv-2603-03780:
Satoshi Oyama, Yuko Sakurai, and Hisashi Kashima design an institution for artificial intelligence agents doing science together. Discovery still leans on individual researchers, wasting effort on redundant trials and shaky reproducibility. Agent teams could explore in parallel, but nearly all studies assume one organization controls every agent, so incentives, sharing, and replication go unexamined. Their 2026 proposal, MACC, treats the institution itself as the research object.

A blackboard-style shared workspace lets independently managed agents post, read, and build on each other's work. Layered incentive mechanisms reward transparency, reproducibility, and efficient exploration rather than raw speed. MACC is offered as a testbed: a place to learn how institutional design shapes collective exploration when the scientists are software. The paper appears in the Blue Sky Ideas track of a leading multi-agent systems conference.
arxiv-2603-03880:
Olga Krestinskaya and others present an approach for co-optimizing in-memory computing accelerators jointly with the workloads they run. Hardware-software co-design matters for these neural network accelerators, but most frameworks target a single workload and produce specialized designs that generalize poorly. Practical deployments instead need one platform that serves many models well.

The framework uses an optimized evolutionary algorithm and captures cross-workload trade-offs explicitly, narrowing the gap between workload-specific and general designs. It is evaluated on both resistive-memory and SRAM-based architectures and proves robust across design scenarios. Optimized designs cut the combined energy-delay-area product sharply compared with baselines, for both small and large workload sets. The result is a practical route to general-purpose in-memory accelerators, and the framework's source code is openly available.
arxiv-2603-03980: Shreya Kumbhakar and others probe puddle motion of an incommensurate charge-density-wave state in 2H-NbSe2, where local order forms only inside confined regions. Raman scattering shows strong Fano contact linking the interlayer shear vibration with the charge-density-wave amplitude mode. Time-resolved reflectivity reveals a low-rate coherent overdamped oscillation near 17 kelvin in the wave regime, pointing toward an unexplored transition. The authors spot a Fano-coupled phonon-wave hybrid from collective puddle motion, clarifying lattice pinning effects.
arxiv-2603-04380: Von Klinski and Schall improve fine grained species reasoning with TaxonRL, a reinforcement learning method. Vision language models struggle to separate similar species in the same genus or family. TaxonRL uses group relative policy optimization with intermediate rewards, forcing hierarchical predictions at species, genus, and family levels before final classification. That structure boosts accuracy and yields transparent, checkable reasoning traces. On Birds-to-Words it reaches 91.7 percent accuracy, above human performance, and generalizes well to primate and marine verification.
arxiv-2603-04680: Singh and colleagues study melting in shocked titanium. Laser shocks with femtosecond x-ray diffraction plus molecular simulations from a learned model probe Ti melting. Runs predict solid-liquid mix along the Hugoniot in the 111 to 124 GPa range. Tests show first signs of liquid at 86 GPa. Grain changes include shrinking tied to liquid arrival, within mix from 110 to 126 GPa. Above 126 GPa, left textured Ti persists to about 180 GPa, well above melt end. The paper covers laser-shock melt onset and end.
arxiv-2603-05080: Karol M. Dąbrowski and team quantify salt precipitation during CO2 injection with microfluidic tests on halite crystallization during brine evaporation in liquid, gaseous, and supercritical phases. The pace is set by transport: the Avrami constant rises by two orders of magnitude as the Peclet number grows. Supercritical CO2 gives the best displacement and the fastest drying, cutting nucleation time from 57 minutes in liquid to under 1 minute in gas or supercritical form. Final crystal fractions rise 10-fold from liquid to gas form, confirming transport and phase state dominate over diffusion.
arxiv-2603-05180: Dimitris Dimitropoulos and colleagues introduce CRISP, a framework for approximate nearest-neighbor search in high-dimensional learned representations. Graph methods grow memory-hungry at thousands of dimensions, and other methods carry heavy preprocessing costs. CRISP redistributes variance only when needed through a lightweight correlation-aware strategy, coupled with a compressed sparse row index. Its dual-mode engine offers a Guaranteed Mode preserving recall bounds and an Optimized Mode cutting latency by rank-weighted scoring and early stopping. Tests at up to 4096 dimensions show throughput, low build costs, and memory efficiency.
arxiv-2603-05280: Ambroise Odonnat and team probe middle layers of pretrained vision transformers across image sorting benchmarks. Middle layers often beat the final layer on discriminative forms. First attributed to autoregressive early training, it also appears under supervised and discriminative self-supervised objectives. Spread shift between early training and downstream data mostly causes deeper-layer degradation. Module analysis shows standard block-output probing is suboptimal. Feedforward-network activations probe best under marked spread shift, while normalized multi-head self-attention output is optimal when shift is weak.
arxiv-2603-05380: Antonio Casares and team describe a history-fixed Büchi automaton using strictly fewer states than any language-equivalent fixed Büchi automaton. This settles a problem open since history-determinism's opening and actively studied for over a decade. Their example has 65 states, and proving its succinctness combines theoretical insights with solvers for NP-complete problems.
arxiv-2603-05580: Colombo and team follow a hint from M. V. Berry to study how superoscillating stand-ins close in on the cut Weierstrass function. The Weierstrass function is the classic example of an unbroken function that is nowhere smooth, built from fast complex powers. They give sharp, clear error bounds for this stand-in and study the tricky closing-in behavior of the linked double limits.
arxiv-2603-05680: Fremling and Hinds present SuperSNEC, a sped-up SuperNova blast code making large radiation-fluid model grids quickly with about 100 zones. The main advance is adjusting gridding, keeping trueness against a 1000-zone base while giving about 420 times speedup. A 100-zone setup hits a gap of 0.022 mag against the 1000-zone base, at under 2 seconds per model. For SN 2011dh, SN 1993J, and SN 2020oi, SuperSNEC finds book-matching settings, with SN 2020oi well matched by a purely radio model.
arxiv-2603-06080: Richardson, McColl, Nilsen, Armstrong, and McCluskey show that quasi-springy neutron scattering can finally settle uneven spinning motion in liquid benzene. Usual fitting often cannot pin down the deep moves, since simple line-shape models let other workings produce same-looking spectra. The team mixes tiny moves models with real derived scattering models that depend on push transfer, Bayes model telling apart, and polar study. Their spinning and tumbling spread numbers point to stronger tilt than before seen, giving a route to the moves behind trapped hydro-carbon speeding.
arxiv-2603-06380: Ganguly and his team extend kinetic based regularization, a local kernel fitting with one tuned parameter, to learn spatial derivatives with second order accuracy in one dimension. Two schemes are proposed: explicit closed form guesses, and an implicit shifted linear system solution. The form enables noise tuned derivative guesses without global system solving or rule of thumb smoothing. Both methods show squared convergence matching finite difference for clean data, with a wider form. Pairing KBR with saving solvers gives stable shock capture in hyperbolic PDEs while keeping conservation laws.
arxiv-2603-06680: Tripathi presents VB, testing whether vision-language models can determine visibility in a photograph and abstain when a viewer cannot answer. Each item pairs one photo with a yes-or-no visibility claim, requiring VISIBLY_TRUE, VISIBLY_FALSE, or ABSTAIN plus a confidence score. VB tests why questions are unanswerable via reason codes, using minimal edits to verify judgments change only when evidence changes. GPT-4o and Gemini 3.1 Pro tie for the best composite score, while Gemma 3 12B, the best open-source model, surpasses one closed-source system.
arxiv-2603-06780: Zaman and colleagues present SpatialMAGIC, a hybrid imputation model for spatial transcriptomics, where gaps and noise hide true signals. It joins MAGIC-based graph diffusion, which captures long-range gene expression links, with transformer-based spatial attention for nearby structure. Filled-in values stay true to place across platforms, and the model beats MAGIC and attention-based rivals on grouping scores. Downstream analyses improve too, with better detection of up- and down-regulated genes and consistent pathway signals.
arxiv-2603-07080: Zheng and colleagues cut the cost of vision-and-language navigation by reusing visual tokens across frames, without retraining. Past caching fails here because the camera moves and the task focus shifts, so position-wise matching pairs the wrong content and cached states go stale. Their VLN-Cache fixes both with view-aligned remapping for geometry and a task-relevance saliency step for focus. The result keeps navigation quality while skipping repeat work.
arxiv-2603-08080: Ebel and colleagues present MRDrive, an open mixed-reality driving simulator built for automotive user research. Building and testing in-car controls needs both ecological validity and experimental control. Current simulators miss that balance. Costly physical rigs resist adaptation. Virtual reality rigs bend more but lose touch with the vehicle. MRDrive blends real and virtual parts so teams can study in-vehicle interaction, attention, and explainability across manual and automated driving.
arxiv-2603-08280: Bovdi and colleagues solve a classification problem for differential operators between spaces of weighted densities in superdimension 1|1. Modular forms and weighted densities over a one-dimensional manifold transform alike under linear fractional changes of coordinates. So classifications of maps between spaces of modular forms and spaces of weighted ones are sometimes identified, although they differ. The authors solve the weighted-density case for superstrings in that superdimension, superizing an earlier result, and offer open problems.
arxiv-2603-08680: Alessandro Cosentino and colleagues offer Metriq, a shared bench for judging quantum computers on equal footing. Scattered tools and uneven methods have blocked fair cross-platform comparison. Metriq unites benchmark design, runs, data, and public display, covers device traits and applied tasks, and pools results from over ten machines into a scored summary.
arxiv-2603-08780: Elisabeth Matthews and colleagues revisit the cold giant Eps Ind Ab with fresh JWST mid-infrared images. The planet glows brighter at 11.3 microns than in a shorter band, a sign of ammonia, though the feature runs shallower than models expect. Their favored read is thick water-ice clouds muting the ammonia and near-infrared light, a pattern echoed across the small sample of cold giants.
arxiv-2603-08980: Doff and de S. Pires compute scalar contributions to the S, T, U precision parameters in a 3-3-1 model. Gauge bosons in this model barely shift the oblique parameters, while the scalar sector had received little attention. Their systematic study finds the T parameter tightly constrains the masses and energy scales of the model's scalar spectrum.
arxiv-2603-09080: Shumin Yao and colleagues run sharp analog joint coding on digital units. Analog coding fades gently across channels, but digital layers produce finite discrete waveforms and non-smooth steps that break gradient flow. Their D2AJSCC uses OFDM subcarrier set as a waveform maker, flipping the digital layer to find bitstreams that mimic analog waves. ProxyNet, a smooth neural stand-in, restores gradient streams for end-to-end training, reaching near-ideal scores with gentle fade.
arxiv-2603-09180: Jianing Yang and colleagues present DuplexCascade, a speech-to-speech dialogue pipeline that keeps cascaded ASR, LLM, and TTS modules yet drops voice activity detection. Cutting long turns into chunk-wise micro-turns allows fast two-way exchange while a strong text model keeps the talk smart. Special control tokens steer turn-taking and reply timing under streaming limits. On two benchmarks it leads open systems in full-duplex turn-taking while holding strong conversational skill.
arxiv-2603-09280: Encarnación Algaba and colleagues study how income might be shared across an endless stream of generations, each endowed with some income of its own. An allocation rule maps each income stream to another, in effect moving income between generations. They show that a family of geometric rules is singled out by axioms of consistency, continuity, and independence. Feasibility and scale invariance serve as the basic requirements behind that characterization.
arxiv-2603-09380: Abdullah Ghani and colleagues reverse-engineer how Meta Pixel is configured across the web with a framework they call PixelConfig. Earlier work mostly counted tracking pixels rather than studying their settings. They examine activity tracking, identity tracking, and tracking restrictions, using Wayback Machine data on 18,000 health-related sites plus a control group of top sites from 2017 to 2024. Early findings show automatic events gathering button clicks and page metadata on many sites.
arxiv-2603-09580: Aleks Kissinger and John van de Wetering introduce ZX-flow, a flexible criterion for extracting deterministic computations from ZX-diagrams. Existing flow criteria were built for graph states, so diagrams must sit in a narrow graph-like form that basic ZX rules easily break. ZX-flow is ZX-native, defined through Pauli semiwebs, a generalization of Pauli webs used in fault-tolerant reasoning. It survives all Clifford rewrites, and a diagram has it exactly when some Clifford-equivalent graph-like diagram carries Pauli flow.
arxiv-2603-09780: Gabriel Stankiewicz, Chaitanya Dev and Paul Steinmann work on sheet designs made by variable thickness topology optimisation. Such designs often gain hard to make thin patches, and their edges blur under the filters the method needs. A combined penalisation and projection step removes nearly all thin patches. Their gradient informed projection then sharpens edges alone, leaving inner form and stiffness almost unchanged.
arxiv-2603-09880: Richard Stiskalek and coauthors redo the Milky Way Cepheid distance calibration with Gaia parallaxes in a fully forward modelled Bayesian frame. The fit solves at once for the period luminosity link, the Gaia zero point offset and each star's distance. Galaxy disc shape and the survey cuts of two Hubble campaigns are built in directly. The results agree closely with the SH0ES values, thanks to the relation's small scatter.
arxiv-2603-09980: Junfeng Liao and coauthors make language model unlearning explainable by giving it an explicit reasoning target. Gradient ascent methods can erase knowledge, yet they also dull general skill, leave gaps and produce incoherent text. Their targeted reasoning unlearning defines both what must go and what the model should say instead. A mix of supervised and ascent losses then removes the set knowledge precisely while sparing other abilities.
arxiv-2603-10080: Ali Raza and coauthors present Amnesia, a lightweight attack that steers internal activations of open weight language models to bypass safety training. Such models can produce harmful content, and alignment methods aim to prevent that. Amnesia manipulates transformer states at chosen layers, needing no fine tuning or extra training. Their red teaming experiments, which include offensive example outputs, show the attack circumvents existing safeguards on leading open models.
arxiv-2603-10380: Divya Gupta and co-authors study a multifield model of the pre-inflationary universe inside loop quantum cosmology. They recast the Hamiltonian dynamics in two equivalent forms, geometrodynamical and Yang-Mills type, with couplings set by the shape of the field space. After polymerization in the stated scheme, they get loop-corrected Friedmann equations. For two-field cases they trace bounce, transition, and slow-roll inflation phases numerically, check e-fold counts for viability, and probe the global flow with stability and dynamical-systems analysis.
arxiv-2603-10680: Daniel J Buxton and co-authors present a platform-agnostic framework for digital human modelling with neurophysiological sensing in game-based interaction. Many such setups are tied to one platform or pipeline, limiting reuse. This work separates sensing, interaction modelling, and inference readiness, giving a base other groups can reuse. An OpenBCI Galea headset supplies EEG, EMG, EOG, PPG, and inertial streams at once, while a SuperTux game supplies the interaction. Signals are stored as time-aligned observables for later AI use under ethical approval.
arxiv-2603-10880: Clement Wong and coauthors ask a question about California drivers. Can drivers of battery electric vehicles feed power back to the grid? Can they do so without harming their batteries or daily routines? The team uses real-world usage data. They group drivers into four profiles, from daily chargers to public chargers. For each profile, they test a user-focused charging strategy. Participation looks most feasible for daily chargers. Battery wear hinges on calendar aging sensitivity. It sometimes even improves retention for drivers who keep batteries highly charged.
arxiv-2603-10980: Zixing Wang and coauthors introduce PPGuide, a lightweight way to steer a pretrained diffusion policy away from failure while it acts. It needs no extra expert demonstrations or learned world model. Attention-based multiple instance learning first labels which observation-action chunks in the policy's own rollouts matter for success or failure. A performance predictor trains on that self-labeled data. At inference time, the predictor's gradient nudges the policy toward more robust actions. Results improve across Robomimic and MimicGen benchmark tasks.
arxiv-2603-11380: Mingzhe Tao and coauthors build a question-answering dataset for the driving scenes autonomous vehicles handle worst. Fog, weather, and failing sensors conspire against perception there. DriveXQA pairs four visual modalities with five sensor failure cases and five weather conditions. It has 102,505 questions at scene, allocentric, and ego-vehicle levels. No existing multimodal model ingests several complementary visual streams. They add MVX-LLM, whose dual cross-attention projector fuses modalities without token bloat. It roughly doubles a baseline's score in fog.
arxiv-2603-11680: Tan and co-authors present UCAN, a lightweight super-resolution network that widens its receptive field without heavy compute. Hybrid designs score well, yet bigger windows or kernels price them out of small devices. UCAN joins window-based spatial attention with Hedgehog Attention to catch local texture and long-range links at once. A distilled large-kernel module keeps high-frequency detail at low cost. On Manga109 at 4x, UCAN-L reaches 31.63 dB PSNR with modest compute, beating recent lightweight rivals.
arxiv-2603-11780: Proboszcz and Cichosz test large language models as classifiers of biomedical articles, across many setups. They vary prompts, output handling, and few-shot example choices, for both open and closed models. The best setups reach average PR AUC above 0.4 with zero-shot prompting, and higher with few-shot prompting. That sits close to naive Bayes, random forest, and fine-tuned transformer scores. Using output token probabilities for class probabilities is one setup they single out as promising.
arxiv-2603-11880: Rajhans and co-authors introduce the Optical Parametric Multi-Pass Cell Amplifier, a hybrid ultrafast laser. Parametric amplifiers tune widely but convert pump power poorly and blur the beam. Multi-pass cell compressors give clean broadband output yet tune little and lose contrast. The new design crosses two multi-pass cells, amplifying seed pulses while wiping the idler each pass. The team reports a record 43% pump-to-signal conversion with a 1030 nm pump at 1 kHz. The 1500 nm signal compresses to 48 fs with strong beam quality and stability.
arxiv-2603-11980: Kai Li and Shiyu Zhao teach robot teams to play laser tag from camera images alone. Their method trains a strong teacher with multi-agent reinforcement learning, then distills it into a vision-based student policy. Two design choices help the student: a permutation-invariant feature extractor and a depth heatmap input. The policy beats classic modular methods on hitting accuracy and collision avoidance, and it runs on real robots.
arxiv-2603-12380: Garuda, Hahn, Bottrell, and Lee make galaxy halo mass inference robust to shifts in simulation physics. HaloFlow reads halo mass from simulated galaxy images with sharp precision. Trained on one physics model, though, it turns biased and overconfident on another. HaloFlow DA adds domain adaptation to the inference frame to fight that shift. Tests span IllustrisTNG, EAGLE, and SIMBA images with two adaptation methods in play. Maximum mean discrepancy works most stably, cutting bias while precision holds, a base for real survey use.
arxiv-2603-13080: Ji-Yu Song and co-authors forecast dark siren cosmology with intermediate-mass black hole binaries seen across three detector bands. Dark sirens probe cosmic expansion, but they need sharp distances and sky spots for galaxy matching. A Taiji, LGWA, and Einstein Telescope network tracks events across bands at once. Simulated samples feed a hierarchical Bayesian frame with catalog gaps and redshift errors in view. The three-band network beat every two-detector pairing they tried. Dark energy limits from sirens alone rivaled current combined probes.
arxiv-2603-13180: Callum McLean and co-authors replace RMSNorm with MXNorm, a norm step that reuses block scales from low-precision casts. Matrix products got fast with new low-precision formats, yet reductions still run in high precision. MXNorm reads the RMS value from the MXFP8 block scales already computed. That shrinks the needed reduction by 32x, with no extra pass. Llama 3 training runs from small to 8B size lost almost no accuracy. Kernel tests also ran faster than the standard norm.
arxiv-2603-13280: Emil Hovad presents SAFE-PIT-CM, an autoencoder for physics-informed tracking in continuum mechanics. Values like thermal diffusivity shape how fields evolve but are hard to measure directly. The model embeds a frozen convolutional layer as a PDE solver in its latent space. Coarse time snapshots can break the von Neumann stability rule for one Euler step. Sub-stepping with SAFE restores stability at negligible cost, since each sub-step is one frozen convolution. On thermal diffusion in metals, it recovered both the coefficient and the field well.
arxiv-2603-13780: Kai Tan and co-authors propose a unified, end-to-end framework for spoofing-robust speaker verification. Such systems must combine speaker verification with a countermeasure against spoofing in one pipeline. Score fusion of separate systems is popular, while single networks are hard to interpret and need retraining for new settings. Their three-class formulation enables log-likelihood ratio inference from class logits, a more interpretable decision path. Results match prior methods on ASVSpoof5 and beat them on SpoofCeleb, they report. Visual analysis backs the interpretability claim.
arxiv-2603-13880: Kaczmarek measures the energy cost of defending neuromorphic chips in edge robots against attacks. The tests run a Hierarchical Temporal Defense setup on a BrainChip Akida AKD1000 processor. Gradient-based attack success falls from about 82 percent to about 19 percent. Timing jitter attacks fall from about 76 percent to about 25 percent. Energy use stays near 45 microjoules per inference. Oddly, the fully defended setup draws less dynamic power, which the author links to sparser network activity.
arxiv-2603-13980: Han and Hu revisit the resource theory of imaginarity and track how three measures decay under noise. The measures are the l1-norm imaginarity, the robustness of imaginarity, and the relative-entropy version. For single-qubit pure states under real channels, the first two decay by one shared channel factor. The entropy measure also depends on how the state sits against the reference basis. Results extend to two-qubit and photonic dual-rail states, linking photon loss to leftover imaginarity.
arxiv-2603-14280: Popescu-Pampu presents an interview with Bernard Teissier, reworked from a recorded conversation. The recording was made at Teissier's house in Paris. Sessions ran over two days, on 28 and 29 September 2024. The published text edits that spoken record into written form. Readers get Teissier's own words, shaped by the interviewer's questions and the later reworking.
arxiv-2603-14480: Hinrichs and co-authors hunt for globular clusters in JWST views of galaxy cluster PLCK G165.7+67.0. They subtract the intracluster light to expose faint point sources. A color-space fit then picks likely cluster members. The team reports over 900 globular cluster candidates from the point source list. A check for interlopers gives a lower estimate of 793, plus or minus 83. The sources track the intracluster light and the lensing mass map. Their brightness curve turns over past the completeness limit.
arxiv-2603-14580: Almeida and Lima study scalaron waves near a BTZ black hole in quadratic f(R) gravity. Pure Einstein gravity in three dimensions has no local moving modes. The f(R) extension turns the Ricci scalar into one such mode, the scalaron. Maxwell-Higgs vortices act as sources for that mode here. The trace equation becomes a massive Klein-Gordon equation for curvature. A Green function gives the profile from any compact source. The response decays with a universal power law and stays stable, they show.
arxiv-2603-14680: May-Mann, Bhattacharjee and Raghu model Hall crystal transitions with composite boson theory. A 2D electron gas in a magnetic field can form three states. The Hall liquid, the Wigner crystal and the Hall crystal cover the options. Composite bosons map them to a superconductor, a Mott insulator and a supersolid. A soft roton in the Hall liquid triggers a first-order jump to a triangular Hall crystal. Softening further melts it into a Wigner crystal in a continuous step. Fractional cases favor honeycomb Hall crystals, they find.
arxiv-2603-14780: Leuenberger and Gunlycke tune electrodynamic forces across screening regimes in one layered setup. A dielectric spacer sits between two gate-tuned 2D conductor sheets. Sheet reflections fully set the field setting. Summing many reflections yields a discrete set of cavity modes. Weak reflection restores bulk power-law forces. Strong reflection splits into two branches by phase. One branch screens with fast decay. The other keeps a gapless mode and can boost the long-range tail.
arxiv-2603-14980: Xu and co-authors measure how impurities shift Coulomb crystallization in laser-cooled ion crystals. Calcium ion crystals host a controlled dose of xenon highly charged ions. The crystallization threshold holds steady at low impurity levels. Past a crossover point, the shift grows near linearly with dose. Local pinning of the crystal around impurities explains the global move. White dwarf and neutron star crystallization models feel the effect. Stellar matter models gain a lab-tested impurity correction. Strongly coupled plasma physics shares the gain.
arxiv-2603-15080: Mandarapu and Kunkunuru build three open biomedical knowledge graphs on Samyama, a graph database written in Rust. One graph covers pathways, one clinical trials, and one drug interactions, drawn from open sources like Reactome and DrugBank. Together they hold about 7.9 million nodes and 28 million edges. All three can load into one tenant for cross-graph joins. A schema-driven tool server lets AI agents query them. On 40 pharmacology questions, these tools reached 98 percent accuracy, beating text-to-Cypher at 85 percent.
arxiv-2603-15480: Molina and co-authors image the 2019 eruption of the symbiotic recurrent nova V3890 Sgr in radio and gamma rays. VLBI maps from day 8 to day 51 show the blast start lopsided, round out, then brighten along the north-south axis. A spherical wind plus a dense ring in the orbital plane explains the shapes. Radio light is mostly synchrotron emission, with a later halo ahead of the shock. Modeling puts gamma rays in the dense ring shocks and radio in the round wind.
arxiv-2603-15580: Becher's thesis builds a low-cost way to model marine biogeochemistry, applied to the Paranagua Estuarine Complex in southern Brazil. Such models track nutrients and water quality but cost much compute and need careful tuning. Her nutrient and phytoplankton model stays simple enough for a home computer. A calibration method pairs tracer data with derivative-free search. Field data then tune the model, which matches the observed nutrient patterns well. The approach extends to seasonal and multi-parameter cases.
arxiv-2603-15680: Schiessl gives a fixed-point method that computes pi to high precision. The method rests on the sine function. A family of update rules is set by one whole-number choice. From a start value near pi, each rule converges to pi. The convergence order is exactly an odd number fixed by that choice. Tests show the scheme runs efficiently in practice. A German version of the text follows the English one.
arxiv-2603-15780: Verninas and co-authors make surface geodesics fast and differentiable on GPU. Learning on curved meshes lacks closed-form tools and smooth discrete operators. Straightest geodesics give a principled route to the exponential map. The team parallelizes that route and derives two gradient paths. One uses an extrinsic proxy function. One uses geodesic finite differences. Tests confirm speed and accuracy gains. A new geodesic convolution layer shows the method in learning pipelines. A mesh flow matching method and a Voronoi optimizer follow.
arxiv-2603-16080: Ghimire, Murad, and Rahimi compare Euclidean and hyperbolic graph networks on Bitcoin data. Transaction graphs encode multi-hop patterns among wallets and entities. Node tasks include entity spotting and transaction class calls. Their study varies neighborhood depth with design held fixed. Tangent-space hyperbolic models face plain Euclidean twins head on. Learning rate and curvature jointly steer hyperbolic training stability. Elliptic data supplies the large test graph for both. The results guide when curved embeddings earn their keep.
arxiv-2603-16380: Belousov, Derkachov, and Khoroshkin build tools for the quantum BC Toda chain. They give an integral form for its wave functions, of Gauss-Givental type. A new reflection operator does key work here. It obeys a reflection equation built from the chain's Lax matrices. The team also defines Baxter operators for this chain. They show those operators commute with the Hamiltonians. A Baxter equation for them follows from the setup.
arxiv-2603-17080: Ayral and co-authors analyze a quadratic optimization problem on the Grassmann manifold from quantum embedding methods. The problem minimizes a trace based quadratic function over matrix subspaces. It is non convex and typically has local minima that are not global. The authors identify cases where the global minimizer comes from an auxiliary convex problem. When that route fails, the auxiliary solution still serves as a strong starting point for other solvers. The motivating use is building bath orbitals.
arxiv-2603-17180: Miotti and co-authors build a mesoscopic model of dynamic Tetra-PEG hydrogel networks. Their hybrid method joins dissipative particle dynamics with Monte Carlo bond exchange. Polymer chains follow a finite extensible elastic potential. Reversible cross links use a Morse potential, with exchange rates set by Bell's force dependent kinetics. After calibration, the model reproduces the Maxwell like viscoelastic response of these gels. Its graph view exposes bond distributions, dangling chain fractions, and cluster sizes that are hard to measure.
arxiv-2603-17280: Chen and co-authors derive a law for how context length sets the energy efficiency of language model inference. They ask how many tokens a GPU cluster delivers per watt. Their answer: tokens per watt halve when the context window doubles. A larger window shrinks how many sequences fit in the KV cache, while power draw stays near flat. They show routing by context length is a stronger lever than newer hardware. A two pool routing scheme gives about 2.5 times the tokens per watt of a fleet.
arxiv-2603-17380: Chen and co-authors present SCALE, a model that predicts how cell populations react to perturbations. Treated and control cells come as unpaired groups, which blocks cell-level matching. SCALE treats cells as unordered sets and learns transport between the groups. It matched gene changes and kept gene targets apart in CRISPR data, they report. Tests on blood samples from three donors backed its cytokine picks.
arxiv-2603-17580: Sahoo and co-authors diagnose why dense retrieval fails on negation in biomedical questions. Contradiction-aware answers need evidence that disputes a claim, not just supports it. Fancy adversarial embeddings collapsed on their proxy tests, scoring near zero. Plain BM25 filtering split the load better, they find. Their decoupled design pairs support recall of 0.810 with contradiction scores of 0.750. At TREC the system placed second on contradiction F1.
arxiv-2603-17680: Du and co-authors build WeatherReasonSeg, a test of reasoning segmentation in bad weather. Most vision-language benchmarks use clean images shot in ideal conditions. Their set adds synthetic rain, snow, and fog at graded levels to known data. A second part curates real storm-weather scenes with mask-guided queries. Scores fall as weather worsens, they find. Each weather type also breaks models in its own pattern. Five reasoning angles widen the check.
